pull.title: wallet: fix persistent coin lock upgrade
pull.body:
Fix a stale persistent coin lock when a temporary coin lock is upgraded to persistent.

Previously, upgrading an existing non-persistent lock to a persistent lock used `emplace()` without updating the existing value. As a result, the in-memory lock remained non-persistent.

When the coin was later spent, `UnlockCoin()` therefore did not erase the persistent `LOCKED_UTXO` database record. After restarting the wallet, the stale lock was loaded again.

This change updates the existing lock state when the coin is already present.

Adds a functional test covering:
- temporary coin lock
- upgrade to persistent lock
- spending the locked coin
- wallet reload
- verification that the spent lock is not restored

Fixes #36304

Maybe your version offers a great UX. This code `src/wallet/rpc/coins.cpp:328:            throw JSONRPCError(RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER, "Invalid parameter, output already locked");` 

```cpp
    if (!fUnlock && is_locked && !persistent) {
            throw JSONRPCError(RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER, "Invalid parameter, output already locked");
        }
```
also supports your solution cause it dictates that we could go from non-persistence to persistence in a single call but not the other way around

Concept ACK on fixing #36304.

Tested `bb5dc52082` against its base, `bb5296576e`.

On the base, the #36304 steps still show the spent coin in `listlockunspent` after `unloadwallet` / `loadwallet`, and `wallet_basic.py` fails with `not(1 == 0)`. On this commit the list stays empty and the test passes.

The other direction looks broken. Lock the coin with `lockunspent` persistent, then spend that same coin. On the base, `listlockunspent` is empty before and after a reload. On this commit it is empty before the reload and the spent output is back afterwards (`gettxout` is null). I got that from both of these:

- `createrawtransaction` of that input, then `fundrawtransaction` with `lockUnspents=true`
- `sendall` with that coin in `inputs` and `lock_unspents=true` (`"complete": true`)

`fundrawtransaction` and `sendall` call `LockCoin(prevout, false)` ([spend.cpp:1543](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/bb5dc52082129001b2c711d3dc1022c380940215/src/wallet/spend.cpp#L1543), [rpc/spend.cpp:1581](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/bb5dc52082129001b2c711d3dc1022c380940215/src/wallet/rpc/spend.cpp#L1581)). `insert_or_assign` sets the in-memory flag to false and leaves the database record. The spend goes through `AddToSpends` to [UnlockCoin](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/bb5dc52082129001b2c711d3dc1022c380940215/src/wallet/wallet.cpp#L801), which skips the erase because the flag is no longer persistent.

A later non-persistent lock should not clear a persistent one. A test for this path would have caught it.

Thanks for the Concept ACK and testing! I didn't go with unlock-then-lock because it requires two RPC calls and isn't atomic — another process could lock the coin in between. The fix updates the existing entry when `emplace` reports the coin was already present, handling the upgrade in a single call and matching the existing behavior in `coins.cpp:328`.

In 8efd73f405bb1c62ef2d2736552f0cfd78cd62eb "wallet: fix persistent coin lock upgrade"

This can use `insert_or_assign` rather than setting the fields afterwards on failed emplacement.
Thanks for the suggestion! I've updated the code to use `insert_or_assign` as suggested.
